=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:506-513 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: `unblock_fixup_origin()` checks only the first line for the fix-up marker, so project-managed fix-up issues with a leading blank line are not recognized.
  WHY: The judge can treat a blocked project-managed fix-up as an ordinary issue and file another fix-up, leaving the fix-up chain uncapped.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:723-727 | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: The fix-up marker detection checks only the first line, so a leading blank line prevents project-managed fix-up issues from being recognized.
  WHY: The judge can file a fix-up of a fix-up, violating the requirement to prevent fix-up chains.
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:560-563 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The assignment `verdict =_read_json(...)` is missing a space after `=`.
  WHY: This is syntactically valid Python and does not fail at runtime; reviewers identify it as a code-style inconsistency.
- scripts/unblock_ledger.py:408-465 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: `latest_automation_rejection()` selects the last matching entry in list order without comparing `created_at`.
  WHY: If comments are not oldest-first, it can select a stale rejection run and leave an item blocked for an extra round.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:494-497 | severity=low | confidence=[2]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: If `unblock_run_ops` fails after posting the regrant marker, the failure log does not identify which operation failed.
  WHY: Operators cannot tell whether the marker comment or a later label operation failed; the reviewer notes the flow remains functionally correct.
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:488 | severity=low | confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The script defaults `ALLOW_WORKFLOW_EDITS` to `false`, while the workflow export defaults it to `true`.
  WHY: If the script is invoked without the workflow export, or a future workflow omits it, the differing defaults can re-deny a stale rejection that would otherwise be granted.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "**Q56: no fix-up of a fix-up.** A blocked issue whose first line is the `ai:unblock-fixup:v1` marker, authored by the pipeline login, gets one `unblock-fixup-<n>` entry in the `ai:operator-step` issue, a `<!-- ai:unblock-fixup-escalated:v1 item=<n> -->` comment and one WARNING."
  expected_change_site: `scripts/unblock_judge.sh:506-513` (`unblock_fixup_origin`) and a regression test exercising the project-managed fix-up body shape produced by `scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:17196-17206`.
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: `unblock_fixup_origin` matches the marker only on the body's first non-empty line, but project-managed fix-up bodies start with `\n` (an empty line) followed by the marker; the Q56 regression tests use `FIXUP_BODY` with the marker as the first line and do not exercise the project-managed body shape.
- requirement: Add a regression test that exercises the project-managed fix-up body shape (leading blank line) so the Q56 fix is not silently lost.
  expected_change_site: `tests/test_unblock_judge.py` near the existing `test_judge_escalates_a_blocked_fixup_instead_of_filing_another` test (line 2282).
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: All four Q56 tests (`test_judge_escalates_a_blocked_fixup_instead_of_filing_another`, `test_failed_fixup_escalation_posts_no_marker_and_no_warning`, `test_judge_escalates_a_fixup_only_once`, `test_untrusted_fixup_marker_is_judged_normally`, lines 2282-2314) use `FIXUP_BODY` with the marker as the first line; no test sets a body that starts with `\n` before the marker.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

  PROBLEM: `unblock_fixup_origin()` reads only the absolute first line of the issue body to detect the fix-up marker, but project-managed fix-up issues created by the poller have a leading blank line.
  WHY: When a project-managed fix-up is blocked, the origin is not detected, so the judge can file another fix-up for the fix-up and defeat the Q56 chain cap.
- scripts/unblock_actions.py:563 (verdict =_read_json(args.verdict_file, "--verdict-file")) | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: There is no space between `=` and `_read_json`.
  WHY: Python accepts this syntax, so it does not fail at runtime; it is inconsistent with the established assignment style.
